sheets.title: GRADING PLAN
sheets.reading_notes: Shows two grading plan options side by side. Option 1 uses 1:1 layback slope; Option 2 uses 2:1 layback slope. Temporary construction access road shown along west side of Building 104. Existing wooden retaining wall at Building 104 / Hall A berm shown. 15' wide temporary construction access road. Underground Hall A structure shown with critical infrastructure note — Radcon must review and approve any excavation inside fence line. Existing underground utilities shown: 8" ABS sanitary sewer (MH 29 connection), 12" DIP waterline, 6" DIP waterline, 15" RCP storm drain. Existing concrete walkway shown. Note indicates soil stockpiling with radiation contamination investigation needed. CAD file: 5866502-C-GRAD PLAN.dwg, plotted Aug 17, 2023 by mcharron. VHB project 58665.02.

sheets.title: PLAN & PROFILE — CROSS SECTION A-A
sheets.reading_notes: Plan view and profile/section for construction access road along west side of Building 104. Shows two options (1:1 and 2:1 slope). Station-based profile showing existing and proposed grades. Key stationing data: 0+96.45 existing fence line; 1+20.96 8" sanitary sewer crossing (elev unknown); 1+27.15 existing 12" DIP waterline crossing (elev unknown); 1+30.12 existing retaining wall BW elev=38.50; 1+34.61 approx exhaust vent; 1+48.65 16" cold piping main transfer line (pipe center elev=50.00); 0+89.84 underground Hall A structure (ground floor elev=3.50); 1+50.30 center of underground truck ramp (ground elev ±8.30). Critical note: Radcon needs to review any excavation of material inside fence line. Fire Line 'min 4 ft below bottom of retaining wall.' CAD file: 5866502-C-PROF.dwg, plotted Aug 17, 2023 by mcharron.

sheets.title: SITE PLAN — STRUCTURAL AND GEOTECHNICAL
sheets.reading_notes: Site plan overlaid with structural and geotechnical narrative text. Structural narrative states: cantilevered reinforced concrete retaining wall system to replace existing wooden wall; foundation is continuous reinforced spread footing approximately 18" thick and 6' wide; wall approximately 16" wide reinforced concrete; drain board on back (soil side) face with drain holes through base to minimize water pressure. Geotechnical: proposed soil boring extraction locations shown on plan. Existing utilities called out including 8" ABS sanitary sewer and 12" DIP waterline west of existing wooden wall, confirmed at least 4' below toe of slope. Recommends private utility locator to investigate and confirm depth, location, size. Note: foundations that support existing pipe adjacent to area of work could be undermined by excavation — structural engineer to provide input to geotechnical and civil. Drainage: 8' of excavation around wall perimeter; 6' wide concrete footer zone plus 6' clear construction access zone. Title block: JEFFERSON LAB - RETAINING WALL, United States Department of Energy, Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility, Newport News VA.

sheets.title: SITE PLAN — ELECTRICAL CONCEPT
sheets.reading_notes: Site plan electrical concept overlay. Key note: 480V, 3-phase circuit (power source and circuit name TBD) to ACCU — circuit will be temporarily removed and capped at limits shown to allow excavation for new retaining wall; circuit shall be reinstalled upon completion of new retaining wall and access road. Existing air-cooled chiller noted — if equipment is mission-critical, recommended to provide a generator to ensure operation during construction. Existing exhaust fan shown — equipment is mission-critical and must remain operational throughout construction. Extensive underground utility network shown including CHW (chilled water), SAN (sanitary), G (gas), COMM (communications), CRYO (cryogenic), CW (cooling water), DIWP (deionized water), and others — consistent with particle accelerator facility utility complexity.
